docTitle: Antony Quentin Roy — Senior Engineering Leader - Quality (QA Ownership)
name: ANTONY QUENTIN ROY
title: ==SENIOR ENGINEERING LEADER – QUALITY==  ·  ==AUTOMATION-FIRST & AI-ENABLED TESTING==

sections.heading: SUMMARY
sections.body: ==Senior Engineering Leader== with **20+ years** in quality engineering and proven track record building, scaling, and leading ==automation-first, AI-driven quality organizations==. Currently Sr. QA Manager at Concord Technologies, embedding quality into engineering workflows and driving ==shift-left quality culture== across enterprise programs. Hands-on technologist who ==owns quality as an engineering discipline==, not a downstream QA function. Expert in ==establishing automation standards across all layers== (unit, API, integration, E2E), ==driving AI-assisted testing adoption==, and ==integrating quality into CI/CD pipelines== at scale. Skilled at ==setting and enforcing quality gates==, defining measurable quality metrics, and ==holding teams accountable== for quality outcomes. Known for ==challenging delivery pressure when quality is at risk== and enabling teams to ship fast **and** reliably. Hands-on with code, testing tools (Selenium, Playwright, API frameworks), and emerging AI testing platforms (GitHub Copilot, RAG, MCP).
sections.note: SCALE & PHILOSOPHY FOCUS — This summary positions you as a quality leader who embeds quality into engineering culture, not a traditional QA manager. Emphasizes: (1) org-wide quality ownership mindset; (2) automation-first philosophy; (3) AI-driven strategy; (4) hands-on technical leadership; (5) accountability and quality gates. Verify: Do you have examples of driving org-level quality culture change? Pushing back on delivery timelines?

note: SENIOR ENGINEERING LEADER — QUALITY FOCUS — This spec emphasizes org-wide quality culture, automation-first philosophy, AI-driven strategy, hands-on technical leadership, and accountability. 75–80% fit. GAPS: (1) Org-scale proof — You've led programs and teams; this role is 250+ engineers. Address by: emphasizing scalability of your frameworks, team coaching at scale, and willingness to grow into org leadership. (2) Hands-on engineering credibility — Ensure you can speak to hands-on testing/automation decisions, not just strategy. (3) Pushing back culture — Highlight examples of standing firm on quality. STRENGTHS: Automation expertise, AI tools knowledge, leadership track record, shift-left mindset, governance experience, mentoring.
